chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abū Bakr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
O Abū Bakr, whatever the sun has shone upon has become tahir (ritually pure).

key_terms.أَشْرَقَتْ: shone or cast its light upon
key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, as the means mentioned for purification
key_terms.يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ: direct address to the narrator Abū Bakr

ai.seo_question: Does sunlight purify things affected by najasah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning taharah, indicating that what the sun shines upon becomes tahir (ritually pure). It appears in the chapter on purifying garments and other things from najasah, showing its relevance to rulings of ritual purity.
